title: 📘 UNIT 4: POPULATION OF AFRICA
notes:
👥 Population → the number of people living in a particular area at a given time.

🌍 Demography → the study of population size, composition, distribution and changes.

⭐ Africa has experienced very rapid population growth, especially since the 1950s.

title: 🌍 4.1 OVERVIEW OF WORLD POPULATION GROWTH AND SIZE
notes:
🌍 World population growth → the increase in the number of people living on Earth over time.

📈 Population growth accelerated greatly after World War II, particularly in less-developed countries.

👥 World population → about 1.6 billion at the beginning of the 20th century and about 6.1 billion by its end.

📊 By the mid-2020 period → the world population had exceeded 7 billion.

⭐ Major reasons for rapid population growth → advances in modern medicine, improved living standards, declining infant and maternal mortality, and increasing life expectancy.

🌍 Population growth and distribution differ considerably between world regions.

📈 Africa's share of world population has increased substantially over time.

title: 👥 AFRICA'S POPULATION SIZE
notes:
🌍 Africa → the world's second-most-populous continent after Asia.

👥 By mid-2020 → Africa had more than 1.3 billion people.

📊 Africa accounted for about 17.5% of the world's population according to the 2021 data used in the textbook.

🌍 Population shares in 2020/2021 included approximately :-
🌏 Asia → 59.4%
🌍 Africa → 17.5%
🇪🇺 Europe → 9.4%
🌎 Latin America & Caribbean → 8.4%
🇺🇸 North America → 4.8%
🌊 Oceania → 0.5%

⭐ Sub-Saharan Africa has one of the world's highest rates of natural population increase.

title: 📈 AFRICA'S POPULATION GROWTH
notes:
📈 Africa's population increased slowly for many centuries but began growing rapidly from about the 1950s.

⏳ 1000–1700 AD → Africa's population took more than 700 years to nearly double.

⏳ After the 1950s → the population took only about 25 years on average to double.

📌 Population doubling time → the time required for a population to double in size.

🧮 Rule of 70 → Doubling Time = 70 ÷ Population Growth Rate.

💡 Example → if growth rate = 2.5%, doubling time = 70 ÷ 2.5 = 28 years.

⭐ Africa's rapid growth is associated with high fertility combined with declining mortality.

title: 🔄 COMPONENTS OF POPULATION CHANGE
notes:
👶 Fertility/Births → increase population.

⚰️ Mortality/Deaths → decrease population.

🚶 Immigration → movement of people into an area; increases population.

🚶‍♀️ Emigration → movement of people out of an area; decreases population.

⭐ Three major components of population change → Fertility, Mortality and Migration.

🌱 Natural increase → Births − Deaths.

🚶 Net migration → Immigrants − Emigrants.

🧮 Demographic balancing equation :-
Population change = Births − Deaths + Immigration − Emigration.

📌 Pt − Po = B − D + I − O.

⭐ Population therefore changes through natural increase and net migration.

title: 🌱 4.2 AFRICA'S MAJOR DEMOGRAPHIC TRENDS
notes:
⭐ Major demographic trends → fertility, mortality, life expectancy and population growth.

👶 Fertility → occurrence of births in a population and a positive factor in population growth.

📊 Total Fertility Rate (TFR) → average number of children a woman would have during her lifetime if current age-specific fertility rates continued throughout her childbearing years (15–49 years).

👶 Crude Birth Rate (CBR) → number of live births per 1,000 mid-year population in a given year.

⚰️ Mortality → occurrence of death in a population and a negative factor affecting population size.

📉 Crude Death Rate (CDR) → number of deaths per 1,000 mid-year population in a given year.

👶 Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) → number of infant deaths before age one per 1,000 live births.

🤰 Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) → maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.

❤️ Life expectancy → average number of years a person can expect to live.

title: 👶 4.2.1 FERTILITY PATTERNS IN AFRICA
notes:
👶 Africa has historically had very high fertility compared with other world regions.

📉 Africa's Total Fertility Rate has declined over recent decades.

📊 TFR → about 5.1 children per woman in 2004 and about 4.7 in 2016; it remained high compared with other world regions.

📊 In 1980 → average African TFR was about 6.6 children per woman.

🌍 Regional variation in TFR in 2020 :-
🇨🇩 Central Africa → 5.8
🌍 Western Africa → 5.1
🌍 Eastern Africa → 4.3
🌍 Northern Africa → 2.9
🌍 Southern Africa → 2.4

⭐ Highest → Central Africa.
⭐ Lowest → Southern Africa.

📌 High fertility is associated with early marriage, early childbearing, limited access to family planning and other social and economic conditions.

title: 👶 FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO HIGH FERTILITY
notes:
📌 Major factors contributing to relatively high fertility in Africa :-

💊 Limited access to contraceptives.
💰 High levels of poverty.
👩 Low status of women.
👨‍🌾 Need for large families as a source of labour.
👶 Children viewed as a symbol of virility.
📚 Low educational background.
👪 Traditions and cultural influences on family size.
💍 Early marriage and early childbearing.

📉 Although fertility is declining, it remains relatively high compared with other world regions.

title: 👶 CRUDE BIRTH RATE IN AFRICA
notes:
👶 Crude Birth Rate → annual live births per 1,000 mid-year population.

🧮 Formula → CBR = (Annual live births ÷ Mid-year population) × 1,000.

📊 Africa's CBR was about 33 births per 1,000 population by mid-2020.

🇸🇴 Somalia → about 49 births/1,000, among the highest in Africa in 2020.

🇲🇺 Mauritius → about 11 births/1,000, among the lowest in Africa in 2020.

⭐ High birth rates contribute strongly to Africa's rapid population growth.

title: ⚰️ 4.2.2 MORTALITY PATTERNS IN AFRICA
notes:
⚰️ Mortality → occurrence of death in a population.

📊 Mortality is measured using :-
1️⃣ Crude Death Rate (CDR)
2️⃣ Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)
3️⃣ Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)
4️⃣ Life Expectancy

📉 Africa's death rate has declined over time.

📊 CDR → about 14 deaths/1,000 in 2007, about 10/1,000 in 2016 and about 8/1,000 by mid-2020.

⚠️ Despite improvement, mortality remains relatively high in some parts of Africa because of limited health services, poor sanitation, disease, poverty, famine, poor nutrition and conflict.

title: 👶 INFANT MORTALITY IN AFRICA
notes:
👶 Infant mortality → death of an infant before the first birthday.

🧮 IMR = (Annual infant deaths ÷ Annual live births) × 1,000.

📊 Africa's IMR → about 47 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2020.

🌍 Regional IMR in 2020 :-
🇨🇫 Central Africa → 62/1,000
🌍 Western Africa → 55/1,000
🌍 Sub-Saharan Africa → 50/1,000
🌍 Eastern Africa → 42/1,000
🌍 Southern Africa → 26/1,000
🌍 Northern Africa → 22/1,000

⭐ Central Africa had the highest rate, while Northern Africa had the lowest.

title: 🤰 MATERNAL MORTALITY
notes:
🤰 Maternal mortality → death related to pregnancy or its management during pregnancy, childbirth or shortly after termination of pregnancy.

📊 Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) → maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.

🧮 MMR = (Maternal deaths ÷ Live births) × 100,000.

⭐ MMR is an important indicator of maternal health and the quality and accessibility of health services.

⚠️ High maternal mortality is associated with inadequate health services and other social and economic difficulties.

title: ❤️ LIFE EXPECTANCY IN AFRICA
notes:
❤️ Life expectancy → number of years a person can expect to live.

👶 Life expectancy at birth → average number of years a newborn is expected to live under current mortality conditions.

📊 Average African life expectancy → about 64 years in 2020.

🌍 Regional differences in 2020 :-
🌍 Northern Africa → 74 years
🌍 Eastern Africa → 66 years
🌍 Southern Africa → 62 years
🌍 Sub-Saharan Africa → 62 years
🌍 Central Africa → 61 years
🌍 Western Africa → 59 years

⭐ Improved medicine, sanitation, vaccines, water supply and health services contribute to increasing life expectancy.

title: 📈 FUTURE POPULATION AND MORTALITY TRENDS
notes:
📈 Africa's population is expected to continue increasing because fertility remains relatively high and mortality has declined.

🌍 African population → projected in the textbook to reach about 2.5 billion by 2050 from about 1.0 billion in 2010.

📉 Population growth rate → expected to decline gradually as fertility falls.

⚰️ Mortality → expected to continue declining with improved medical technology, sanitation, medicines, vaccines and health services.

👶 Child mortality → projected to decline as incomes, water supply, sanitation and health facilities improve.

⭐ Reduced mortality and increasing life expectancy will gradually contribute to population ageing.

title: 👥 4.3 POPULATION STRUCTURE
notes:
👥 Population structure → composition of a population according to characteristics such as age and sex.

🎂 Age structure → distribution of people into different age groups.

🚹🚺 Sex structure → distribution of males and females in a population.

📊 Population pyramid → graphical representation of the age-sex composition of a population.

⭐ African population structure is characterized by a large young population and a relatively small elderly population.

📌 Major age groups → Young (0–14), Working age (15–64), Old age (65+).

title: 🎂 AGE STRUCTURE OF AFRICA
notes:
🎂 Age structure → distribution of a population among young, working-age and old-age groups.

🌍 Africa has a predominantly young population.

📊 Africa's median age → about 19.7 years in mid-2020.

📌 Low median age → generally indicates high fertility and rapid population growth.

📌 High median age → generally indicates lower fertility and slower population growth.

📊 Africa's population by age in 2020 :-
👶 Young (0–14) → 41%
👷 Working age (15–64) → 56%
👴 Old (65+) → 3%

⚠️ A large young population increases demand for food, education, health care, employment, housing and other services.

title: ⚖️ AGE DEPENDENCY RATIO
notes:
⚖️ Age Dependency Ratio (ADR) → relationship between dependent age groups and the working-age population.

👶 Dependents → mainly young people aged 0–14 and older people aged 65+.

👷 Working population → people aged 15–64.

📊 Africa's ADR in 2020 → about 78.6 dependents per 100 working-age people.

🌍 Central Africa → highest ADR at about 96.1.

🌍 Southern Africa → lowest ADR at about 53.8.

⭐ High dependency means a relatively large share of the population depends on the working-age population for support.

title: 🚹🚺 SEX STRUCTURE AND SEX RATIO
notes:
🚹🚺 Sex structure → composition of a population according to males and females.

⚖️ Sex ratio → number of males for every 100 females in a population.

🧮 Sex Ratio = (Male population ÷ Female population) × 100.

💡 Example → 3.6 million males and 4 million females gives a sex ratio of 90, meaning 90 males for every 100 females.

⭐ Sex structure can influence marriage rates, fertility, occupational structure and population growth.

title: 📊 POPULATION PYRAMID
notes:
📊 Population pyramid → graph showing the age-sex composition of a population.

👦 Males → normally shown on the left side.
👧 Females → normally shown on the right side.

🎂 Age groups → arranged vertically from younger to older ages.

📏 Bar length → represents the number or percentage of males/females in each age group.

📌 Population pyramids commonly use five-year age groups.

⭐ Population pyramids help identify fertility, mortality, life expectancy, population growth and dependency patterns.

title: 🔺 TYPES OF POPULATION PYRAMIDS
notes:
1️⃣ 🔺 Expansive Pyramid → broad base, many children, high fertility, rapid population growth, relatively few older people and generally lower life expectancy.

2️⃣ 🔻 Constructive Pyramid → narrower base, fewer young people and a larger proportion of older people; commonly associated with ageing populations and developed countries.

3️⃣ ⬜ Stationary Pyramid → relatively balanced fertility and mortality, producing little or zero population growth.

⭐ Most developing countries, including much of Africa, are characterized by expansive pyramids with broad bases and narrowing tops.

📌 Broad base → high fertility.
📌 Narrowing toward the top → increasing mortality with age and lower life expectancy.

title: 🌍 CHARACTERISTICS OF AFRICAN POPULATION STRUCTURE
notes:
⭐ Major characteristics of African population :-

👶 High fertility.
⚰️ Historically high mortality, although declining.
👥 Predominantly young population.
🔺 Generally triangular/expansive population pyramid.
⚖️ High age dependency ratio.
👶 High youth dependency.
👴 Low old-age dependency.
❤️ Relatively low life expectancy compared with developed regions.
📈 High population growth rate.

⚠️ A young and rapidly growing population creates both opportunities and strong demands for education, employment, health care, food and infrastructure.

title: 📍 4.4 DISTRIBUTION AND DENSITY OF AFRICA'S POPULATION
notes:
📍 Population distribution → the way people are spread over the Earth's surface.

👥 Population density → number of people living per unit area of land.

🌍 Africa's population distribution is highly uneven.

🏜️ Vast Sahara → very few permanent residents.

🌾 Nile Valley of Egypt, Mauritius, Rwanda and Burundi → among the densely populated areas.

📊 Africa's average crude population density in 2019 → about 44 people/km².

⭐ Being highly populous does not necessarily mean being densely populated.

title: 🌍 FACTORS AFFECTING POPULATION DISTRIBUTION IN AFRICA
notes:
🌦️ Physical factors :-
☀️ Climate
🏔️ Relief
💧 Availability of water
🌱 Soil fertility
⛏️ Distribution of minerals

👥 Human factors :-
💰 Economic conditions
🏛️ Political conditions
👪 Social factors
🏭 Employment and economic opportunities

⭐ Areas with favorable environmental and economic conditions generally attract more people, while harsh environments such as deserts support fewer permanent residents.

title: 📊 REGIONAL POPULATION DENSITY OF AFRICA
notes:
📊 Crude population density by major African regions, 2019 :-

🌍 Western Africa → 65 people/km²
🌍 Eastern Africa → 65 people/km²
🌍 Sub-Saharan Africa → 49 people/km²
🌍 Northern Africa → 31 people/km²
🌍 Central Africa → 27 people/km²
🌍 Southern Africa → 25 people/km²
🌍 Africa → 44 people/km²

⭐ Highest regional density → Western and Eastern Africa.
⭐ Lowest regional density → Southern Africa.

📌 Most populous countries mentioned → Nigeria, Ethiopia, Egypt, DRC and South Africa.

📌 Among the most densely populated countries → Mauritius, Rwanda, Burundi, Comoros and Seychelles.

title: 🏙️ 4.5 URBAN AND RURAL SETTLEMENT PATTERNS IN AFRICA
notes:
🏘️ Settlement → a place where people live and establish homes and communities.

🌾 Rural settlement → settlement mainly associated with countryside and agricultural areas.

🏙️ Urban settlement → settlement associated with towns and cities and a concentration of population and economic activities.

🏙️ Urbanization → growth in the proportion of people living in urban areas.

🌍 Africa has major differences in urbanization between countries and regions.

📈 Urban growth is strongly associated with migration from rural areas to cities.

⭐ Rapid urbanization creates increasing demand for land, infrastructure, housing, health services and other basic services.

title: 🏙️ URBANIZATION IN AFRICA
notes:
📊 About 41% of Africa's population was estimated to live in urban areas according to the data used in the textbook.

🌍 Regional urban population in 2016 :-
🌍 Southern Africa → 62%
🌍 Northern Africa → 51%
🌍 Central Africa → 47%
🌍 Western Africa → 45%
🌍 Eastern Africa → 26%

⭐ Most urbanized region → Southern Africa.
⭐ Least urbanized region → Eastern Africa.

🇬🇦 Gabon → nearly 90% of its population was urban according to the textbook's cited data.

🇧🇮 Burundi → about 12% urban, among the least urbanized countries.

title: 🌆 MAJOR AFRICAN MEGACITIES
notes:
🏙️ Megacity → city with a population of more than 10 million.

⭐ Seven African megacities identified in the textbook :-
🇪🇬 Cairo
🇨🇩 Kinshasa
🇳🇬 Lagos
🇬🇭 Accra
🇿🇦 Johannesburg–Pretoria
🇸🇩 Khartoum
🇰🇪 Nairobi

📈 Rapid urban growth increases the need for housing, transportation, water, sanitation, electricity, employment and health services.

title: ⚠️ POPULATION GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT CHALLENGES
notes:
📈 Rapid population growth creates both opportunities and challenges.

⚠️ Major challenges include :-
🍚 Producing enough food.
💧 Increasing freshwater scarcity.
🏥 Providing adequate health care.
📚 Expanding education.
🏠 Providing sufficient housing.
💼 Creating employment.
🌱 Preventing environmental degradation.
🚶 Managing migration and emigration.
🏗️ Expanding infrastructure.

⭐ A large young population can provide a future labor force, but only if adequate education, skills, employment and infrastructure are provided.

title: 🏙️ URBANIZATION: OPPORTUNITIES AND PROBLEMS
notes:
🏙️ Urbanization can create opportunities through concentration of economic activities, employment, services and infrastructure.

⚠️ Rapid and poorly managed urban growth can create :-
🏚️ Housing shortages.
🚗 Traffic congestion.
💧 Pressure on water supply.
🚽 Sanitation problems.
🏥 Pressure on health services.
🏗️ Infrastructure shortages.
💰 Urban poverty.

🌾 Rapid urban growth can also depopulate rural areas and reduce agricultural labor availability.

⭐ Planned urban development is important for managing population growth and improving living conditions.

title: 🧠 UNIT 4 KEY TERMS
notes:
👥 Population → number of people living in a given area.

🌍 Demography → study of population characteristics and changes.

📈 Population growth → increase in population size over time.

⏳ Population doubling time → time required for population to double.

👶 Fertility → occurrence of births in a population.

📊 TFR → average number of children a woman would have during her lifetime under current fertility conditions.

👶 CBR → annual live births per 1,000 mid-year population.

⚰️ Mortality → occurrence of deaths in a population.

⚰️ CDR → annual deaths per 1,000 mid-year population.

👶 IMR → infant deaths before age one per 1,000 live births.

🤰 MMR → maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.

❤️ Life expectancy → expected average number of years a person will live.

🌱 Natural increase → births minus deaths.

🚶 Net migration → immigration minus emigration.

🎂 Age structure → population distribution by age groups.

🚹🚺 Sex structure → population composition by sex.

⚖️ Sex ratio → males per 100 females.

📊 Population pyramid → graph showing age-sex composition.

⚖️ Age dependency ratio → relationship between dependent and working-age populations.

📍 Population distribution → spatial arrangement of people.

👥 Population density → number of people per unit area.

🏘️ Settlement → place where people live.

🏙️ Urbanization → increase in the proportion of people living in urban areas.
